courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour; outside study, seven hours. Description of basic semiconductor materials for device processing; preparation and characterization of silicon, III-V compounds, and films. Discussion of principles of CVD, MOCVD, LPE, and MBE; metals and dielectrics. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Phase Relations in Solids
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour; outside study, seven hours. Summary of thermodynamic laws, equilibrium criteria, solution thermodynamics, mass-action law, binary and ternary phase diagrams, glass transitions. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Diffusion and Diffusion-Controlled Reactions
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour; outside study, seven hours. Diffusion in metals and ionic solids, nucleation and growth theory; precipitation from solid solution, eutectoid decomposition, design of heat treatment processes of alloys, growth of intermediate phases, gas-solid reactions, design of oxidation-resistant alloys, recrystallization, and grain growth. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Diffusion and Diffusion-Controlled Reactions Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory, two hours; outside study, four hours. Design of heat-treating cycles and performing experiments to study interdiffusion, growth of intermediate phases, recrystallization, and grain growth in metals. Analysis of data. Comparison of results with theory. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Structure and Properties of Metallic Alloys
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; outside study, eight hours. Physical metallurgy of steels, lightweight alloys (Al and Ti), and superalloys. Strengthening mechanisms, microstructural control methods for strength and toughness improvement. Grain boundary segregation. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Materials Selection and Engineering Design A
courses.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, two hours; outside study, five hours. Explicit guidance among myriad materials available for design in engineering. Properties and applications of steels, nonferrous alloys, polymeric, ceramic, and composite materials, coatings. Materials selection, treatment, and serviceability emphasized as part of successful design. Design projects. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Materials Selection and Engineering Design B
courses.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, two hours; outside study, five hours. Explicit guidance among myriad materials available for design in engineering. Properties and applications of steels, nonferrous alloys, polymeric, ceramic, and composite materials, coatings. Materials selection, treatment, and serviceability emphasized as part of successful design. Design projects. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Computer Methods and Instrumentation in Materials Science
courses.prereq_text: Limited to junior/senior Materials Science and Engineering majors
courses.description: Laboratory, four hours. Preparation: knowledge of BASIC or C or assembly language. Interface and control techniques, real-time data acquisition and processing, computer-aided testing. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour; outside study, seven hours. Plastic flow of metals under simple and combined loading, strain rate and temperature effects, dislocations, fracture, microstructural effects, mechanical and thermal treatment of steel for engineering applications. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Mechanical Behavior Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory, four hours. Methods of characterizing mechanical behavior of various materials; elastic and plastic deformation, fracture toughness, fatigue, and creep. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Introduction to Polymers
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour; outside study, seven hours. Polymerization mechanisms, molecular weight and distribution, chemical structure and bonding, structure crystallinity, and morphology and their effects on physical properties. Glassy polymers, springy polymers, elastomers, adhesives. Fiber forming polymers, polymer processing technology, plasticiation. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Structure and Properties of Composite Materials
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; outside study, eight hours. Preparation: at least two courses from 132, 143A, 150, 160. Relationship between structure and mechanical properties of composite materials with fiber and particulate reinforcement. Properties of fiber, matrix, and interfaces. Selection of macrostructures and material systems. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Introduction to Ceramics and Glasses
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour; outside study, seven hours. Introduction to ceramics and glasses being used as important materials of engineering, processing techniques, and unique properties. Examples of design and control of properties for certain specific applications in engineering. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Processing of Ceramics and Glasses
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Study of processes used in fabrication of ceramics and glasses for structural applications, optics, and electronics. Processing operations, including modern techniques of powder synthesis, greenware forming, sintering, glass melting. Microstructure properties relations in ceramics. Fracture analysis and design with ceramics. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Laboratory in Ceramics
courses.comments: Recommended corequisite: course 161.
courses.description: Laboratory, four hours. Processing of common ceramics and glasses. Attainment of specific properties through process control for engineering applications. Quantitative characterization and selection of raw materials. Slip casting and extrusion of clay bodies. Sintering of powders. Glass melting and fabrication. Determination of chemical and physical properties. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Electronic Ceramics
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; outside study, eight hours. Utilization of ceramics in microelectronics; thick film and thin film resistors, capacitors, and substrates; design and processing of electronic ceramics and packaging; magnetic ceramics; ferroelectric ceramics and electro-optic devices; optical wave guide applications and designs. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Electrochemical Processes
courses.prereq_text: course 130 (or Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering 105A), Chemical Engineering 102B
courses.description: (Same as Chemical Engineering CM114.) Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour; outside study, seven hours. Fundamentals of electrochemistry and engineering applications to industrial electrochemical processes. Primary emphasis on fundamental approach to analyze electrochemical processes. Specific topics include electrochemical reactions on metal and semiconductor surfaces, electrodeposition, electroless deposition, electrosynthesis, fuel cells, aqueous and non-aqueous batteries, solid-state electrochemistry. May be concurrently scheduled with course CM263. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Engaging Elements of Communication: Oral Communication
courses.description: Lecture, one hour; discussion, one hour; outside study, four hours. Comprehensive oral presentation and communication skills provided by building on strengths of individual personal styles in creation of positive interpersonal relations. Skill set prepares students for different types of academic and professional presentations for wide range of audiences. Learning environment is highly supportive and interactive as it helps students creatively develop and greatly expand effectiveness of their communication and presentation skills. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Engaging Elements of Communication: Writing for Technical Community
courses.description: Lecture, one hour; discussion, one hour; outside study, four hours. Comprehensive technical writing skills on subjects specific to field of materials science and engineering. Students write review term paper in selected subject field of materials science and engineering from given set of journal publications. Instruction leads students through several crucial steps, including brainstorming, choosing title, coming up with outline, concise writing of abstract, conclusion, and final polishing. Other subjects include writing style, word choices, and grammar. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Introduction to Biomaterials
courses.description: (Same as Bioengineering CM178.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours; outside study, seven hours. Engineering materials used in medicine and dentistry for repair and/or restoration of damaged natural tissues. Topics include relationships between material properties, suitability to task, surface chemistry, processing and treatment methods, and biocompatibility. Concurrently scheduled with course CM280. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Special Courses in Materials Science and Engineering
courses.description: Seminar, four hours; outside study, eight hours. Special topics in materials science and engineering for undergraduate students taught on experimental or temporary basis, such as those taught by resident and visiting faculty members. May be repeated once for credit with topic or instructor change. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Research Group Seminars: Materials Science and Engineering
courses.description: Seminar, four hours; outside study, eight hours. Designed for undergraduate students who are part of research group. Discussion of research methods and current literature in field or of research of faculty members or students. May be repeated for credit. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MAT SCI
courses.title: Directed Research in Materials Science and Engineering
courses.description: Tutorial, to be arranged. Supervised individual research or investigation under guidance of faculty mentor. Culminating paper or project required. Occasional field trips may be arranged. May be repeated for credit with school approval. Individual contract required; enrollment petitions available in Office of Academic and Student Affairs. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Precalculus
courses.prereq_text: successful completion of Mathematics Diagnostic Test
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Preparation: three years of high school mathematics. Function concept. Linear and polynomial functions and their graphs, applications to optimization. Inverse, exponential, and logarithmic functions. Trigonometric functions. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus for Life Sciences Students
courses.prereq_text: successful completion of Mathematics Diagnostic Test (score of 48 or better) or course 1 with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Preparation: three and one half years of high school mathematics (including trigonometry). Not open for credit to students with credit in another calculus sequence. Modeling with functions, limits, and derivatives, decisions and optimization in biology, derivative rules and tools. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus for Life Sciences Students
courses.prereq_text: course 3A with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 31B. Applications of differentiation, integration, differential equations, linear models in biology, phase lines and classifying equilibrium values, bifurcations. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Ordinary Differential Equations with Linear Algebra for Life Sciences Students
courses.prereq_text: course 3B with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Multivariable modeling, matrices and vectors, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, linear and nonlinear systems of differential equations, probabilistic applications of integration. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Transition to Upper Division Mathematics
courses.description: (Formerly numbered 95.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 131A or 132. Introduction to writing and evaluating rigorous mathematical proofs. Covers basic logic; structure of mathematical proofs; sets, functions; natural numbers and induction; axiomatic systems; orderings and equivalence relations; topology of the real numbers; sequences and convergence. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Gateway to Mathematics: Number Theory
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introductory number theory course for freshmen and sophomores. Topics include prime number theory and cryptographic applications, factorization theory (in integers and Gaussian integers), Pythagorean triples, Fermat descent (for sums of squares and Fermat quartic), Pell’s equation, and Diophantine approximation. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Fiat Lux Freshman Seminars
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Discussion of and critical thinking about topics of current intellectual importance, taught by faculty members in their areas of expertise and illuminating many paths of discovery at UCLA. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential and Integral Calculus
courses.prereq_text: successful completion of Mathematics Diagnostic Test or course 1 with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Preparation: at least three and one half years of high school mathematics (including some coordinate geometry and trigonometry). Differential calculus and applications; introduction to integration. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential and Integral Calculus Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: successful completion of Mathematics Diagnostic Test or course 1 with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; laboratory, one hour. Preparation: at least three and one-half years of high school mathematics (including some coordinate geometry and trigonometry). Not open for credit to students with credit for course 31A. Intended for students who still need to review precalculus material (laboratory) while starting calculus. Differential calculus and applications; introduction to integration. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Integration and Infinite Series
courses.prereq_text: course 31A with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 3B. Transcendental functions; methods and applications of integration; sequences and series. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Integration and Infinite Series (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: course 31A with grade of B or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Honors course parallel to course 31B. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus for Economics Students
courses.prereq_text: course 31A with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 3B, 3C, or 31B. Calculus for applications to economics. Partial differentiation, implicit functions, exponential and logarithmic functions, extrema, optimization, constrained optimization. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus of Several Variables
courses.prereq_text: course 31A with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to differential calculus of several variables, vector field theory. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus of Several Variables (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: course 31A with grade of B or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Honors course parallel to course 32A. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus of Several Variables
courses.prereq_text: courses 31B and 32A, with grades of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to integral calculus of several variables, line and surface integrals. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus of Several Variables (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: courses 31B and 32A, with grades of B or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Honors course parallel to course 32B. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Essential Calculus for Mathematical Biologists
courses.description: (Same as Computational and Systems Biology M32 and Life Sciences M32.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open to students with credit for course 31A, 31B, 32A, or 32B. Designed for life sciences students. Methods and results of single and multivariable calculus essential for quantitative training in biology. Limits, differentiation (single and several variables), optimization, integration and methods of integration, Taylor polynomials and applications to approximation, Taylor and other power series, vector valued functions, gradients, and Lagrange multipliers. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra and Applications
courses.prereq_text: course 3B or 31B or 32A with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to linear algebra: systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, linear independence, subspaces, bases and dimension, orthogonality, least-squares methods, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, matrix diagonalization, and symmetric matrices. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra and Applications (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: course 3B or 31B or 32A with grade of B or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Honors course parallel to course 33A. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.prereq_text: course 31B with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Highly recommended: course 33A. First-order, linear differential equations; second-order, linear differential equations with constant coefficients; power series solutions; linear systems. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Data-Driven Mathematical Modeling: Life, Universe, and Everything
courses.prereq_text: courses 31A, 31B, 32A, 32B, 33A, one statistics course from Statistics 10, 12, 13, one programming course from Computer Science 31, Program in Computing 10A, Statistics 20
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to data-driven mathematical modeling combing data analysis with mechanistic modeling of phenomena from various applications. Topics include model formulation, data visualization, nondimensionalization and order-of-magnitude physics, introduction to discrete and continuous dynamical systems, and introduction to discrete and continuous stochastic models. Examples drawn from many fields and practice problems from Mathematical Contest in Modeling. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Discrete Structures
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 180 or 184. Discrete structures commonly used in computer science and mathematics, including sets and relations, permutations and combinations, graphs and trees, induction. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Probability
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to probability through applications and examples. Topics include laws of large numbers, statistics, chance trees, conditional probability, Bayes’ rule, continuous and discrete random variables, jointly distributed random variables, multivariate normal and conditional distributions. In-depth discussion of betting schemes in gambling, occurrence of rare events, coincidences, and statistical predictions. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Key Issues in K-12 Mathematics
courses.description: Seminar, two hours; fieldwork (classroom observation and participation), two hours. Introduction to K-12 mathematics activity in the U.S. Cultivation of interest in teaching through exploration of the sequences of mathematical content and habits of mind taught in these grades. Analysis of sequences of topics in the current California State Standards in Mathematics (CCSS-M), the mathematical structures that underlie these sequences, and cognitive aspects of learning mathematics. Experience with professional mathematician’s habits of mind outlined in the California Standards for Mathematical Practice (including proof and mathematical modeling) and effective strategies for teaching mathematics to diverse student groups. Fieldwork in local mathematics classrooms arranged by Cal Teach program. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics and Pedagogy for Teaching Elementary Mathematics
courses.description: Seminar, two hours; fieldwork (classroom observation and participation), two hours. Facilitates development of professional mathematical and pedagogical understandings required to teach California’s K-5 mathematics curriculum. Exploration of K-5 mathematics, practice of effective teaching strategies for all learners, and discussion of current research and standards in mathematics education. Fieldwork in local mathematics classrooms (observation and presentation of lesson plan) arranged by Cal Teach program. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics and Pedagogy for Teaching Middle School Mathematics
courses.description: Seminar, two hours; fieldwork (off-campus classroom observation and participation), two hours. Facilitates development of professional mathematical and pedagogical understandings required to teach California middle school mathematics curriculum. Exploration of topics in grades six through eight mathematics from a professional perspective, practice with effective teaching strategies for all learners, and discussion of current research and standards in mathematics education. Clinical practice in local mathematics classrooms arranged by Cal Teach program. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Honors Seminars
courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Designed as adjunct to lower-division lecture course. Exploration of topics in greater depth through supplemental readings, papers, or other activities and led by lecture course instructor. May be applied toward honors credit for eligible students. Honors content noted on transcript. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Honors Contracts
courses.prereq_text: Limited to students in College Honors Program
courses.description: Tutorial, three hours. Designed as adjunct to lower-division lecture course. Individual study with lecture course instructor to explore topics in greater depth through supplemental readings, papers, or other activities. May be repeated for maximum of 4 units. Individual honors contract required. Honors content noted on transcript. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Outreach: Explorations of Mathematics in the Physical World
courses.description: Lecture, twelve hours; discussion one hour. Preparation: three years of high school mathematics (to algebra II), some basic familiarity with computers. Uses inquiry-based mathematical modeling as a tool for understanding dynamics of physical systems and chemical processes. Fundamental concepts of single-variable calculus and models of dynamical processes in physics, chemistry, and other subjects in which quantities change with time. Use of computer program C++ for problem solving, plotting, and dynamical simulation in the laboratory. Exploration of current topics in metacognition and education research focused on methods of learning and their practical application in small-group settings. Students practice communication skills with frequent assessment of and feedback on progress. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Variable Topics in Mathematics
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Study of selected topics in mathematics at introductory level. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: PEERS Collaborative Learning Workshops for Life Sciences Majors
courses.prereq_text: (associated undergraduate lecture course in mathematics for life sciences majors) (may be taken concurrently); and Limited to Program for Excellence in Education and Research in Science (PEERS) students
courses.description: Laboratory, three hours. Development of intuition and problem-solving skills in collaborative learning environment. May be repeated four times, but only 1 unit may be applied toward graduation. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: PEERS Collaborative Learning Workshops for Physical Sciences and Engineering Majors
courses.prereq_text: (associated undergraduate lecture course in mathematics for physical sciences and engineering majors) (may be taken concurrently); and Limited to Program for Excellence in Education and Research in Science (PEERS) students
courses.description: Laboratory, three hours. Development of intuition and problem-solving skills in collaborative learning environment. May be repeated four times, but only 1 unit may be applied toward graduation. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Student Research Program
courses.description: Tutorial (supervised research or other scholarly work), three hours per week per unit. Entry-level research for lower-division students under guidance of faculty mentor. Students must be in good academic standing and enrolled in minimum of 12 units (excluding this course). Individual contract required; consult Undergraduate Research Center. May be repeated. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Problem Solving
courses.prereq_text: course 31A with grade of C– or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Problem-solving techniques and mathematical topics useful as preparation for Putnam Examination and similar competitions. Continued fractions, inequalities, modular arithmetic, closed form evaluation of sums and products, problems in geometry, rational functions and polynomials, other nonroutine problems. Participants expected to take Putnam Examination. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Problem Solving
courses.prereq_text: course 100 or significant experience with mathematical competitions
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Enrollment based on one selection test or past Putnam results. Advanced problem solving techniques and mathematical topics useful as preparation for Putnam competition. Problems in abstract algebra, linear algebra, number theory, combinatorics, probability, real and complex analysis, differential, equations, Fourier analysis. Regular practice tests given, similar in difficulty to Putnam competition. May be repeated for maximum of 12 units. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics and Pedagogy for Teaching Middle School Mathematics
courses.comments: requisite to 103B, which is enforced requisite to 103C.
courses.description: Seminar, one hour; fieldwork (classroom observation and participation), two hours. Course 103A is enforced Facilitates student development in mathematical and pedagogical understandings required to teach middle school mathematics curriculum. Exploration of California’s grades 6 through 8 mathematics from professional perspective, practice with effective teaching strategies for all learners, and discussion of current research and standards in mathematics education with fieldwork in local mathematics classrooms. P/NP (undergraduates) or S/U (graduates) grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Observation and Participation: Mathematics Instruction
courses.description: Seminar, one hour; fieldwork (classroom observation and participation), two hours. Observation, participation, or tutoring in mathematics classes at middle school and secondary levels. May be repeated for credit. P/NP (undergraduates) or S/U (graduates) grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Observation and Participation: Mathematics Instruction
courses.description: Seminar, one hour; fieldwork (classroom observation and participation), two hours. Observation, participation, or tutoring in mathematics classes at middle school and secondary levels. May be repeated for credit. P/NP (undergraduates) or S/U (graduates) grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics and Pedagogy for Teaching Secondary School Mathematics
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; fieldwork, 30 minutes. Highly recommended: course 73XP. Facilitates student development of the domains of mathematical knowledge for teaching high school mathematics including common, specialized, and horizon content knowledge as well as relationships between this knowledge and students, teaching, and curriculum. Focus on definition, properties, applications, and modeling with polynomial, rational functions, exponential, and logarithmic functions, including solutions of equations arising in modeling and mathematical contexts. Algebraic structure of the reals and complexes, and polynomial and rational expressions. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics and Pedagogy for Teaching Secondary School Mathematics
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; fieldwork, 30 minutes. Facilitates student development of the domains of mathematical knowledge for teaching high school mathematics including common, specialized, and horizon content knowledge as well as relationships between this knowledge and students, teaching, and curriculum. Focus on topics in trigonometry and geometry including circular functions; solving equations arising from circular functions; trigonometric identities; Euclidean, spherical, and hyperbolic geometries; plane transformations; congruence and similarity; group structure of transformations. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics and Pedagogy for Teaching Secondary School Mathematics
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; fieldwork, 30 minutes. Development of the domains of mathematical knowledge for teaching high school mathematics including common, specialized, and horizon content knowledge as well as relationships between this knowledge and students, teaching, and curriculum. Focus on topics in single variable calculus including deriving and applying results related to limits, difference quotients, derivatives, Riemann sums, and integrals. Focus on topics in statistics including analysis of categorical and quantitative variables; inference from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; and calculating expected values to solve problems. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: History of Mathematics
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Roots of modern mathematics in ancient Babylonia and Greece, including place value number systems and proof. Development of algebra through Middle Ages to Fermat and Abel, invention of analytic geometry and calculus. Selected topics. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 117. Ring of integers, integral domains, fields, polynomial domains, unique factorization. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra (Honors)
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Honors course parallel to course 110A.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Groups, structure of finite groups. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra (Honors)
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Honors course parallel to course 110B.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Field extensions, Galois theory, applications to geometric constructions, and solvability by radicals.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Theory of Numbers
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Algebraic number theory (including prime ideal theory), cyclotomic fields and reciprocity laws, Diophantine equations (especially quadratic forms, elliptic curves), equations over finite fields, topics in theory of primes, including prime number theorem and Dirichlet’s theorem. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Computability Theory
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Effectively calculable, Turing computable, and recursive functions; Church/Turing thesis. Normal form theorem; universal functions; unsolvability and undecidability results. Recursive and recursively enumerable sets; relative recursiveness, polynomial-time computability. Arithmetical hierarchy. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Logic
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to mathematical logic, aiming primarily at completeness and incompleteness theorems of Gödel. Propositional and predicate logic; syntax and semantics; formal deduction; completeness, compactness, and Lowenheim/Skolem theorems. Formal number theory: nonstandard models; Gödel incompleteness theorem. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Set Theory
courses.description: (Same as Philosophy M134.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Axiomatic set theory as framework for mathematical concepts; relations and functions, numbers, cardinality, axiom of choice, transfinite numbers. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. Techniques of proof, abstract vector spaces, linear transformations, and matrices; determinants; inner product spaces; eigenvector theory. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: course 33A with grade of B or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. Honors course parallel to course 115A. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Linear transformations, conjugate spaces, duality; theory of a single linear transformation, Jordan normal form; bilinear forms, quadratic forms; Euclidean and unitary spaces, symmetric skew and orthogonal linear transformations, polar decomposition. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Cryptology
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for Program in Computing 130. Introduction to mathematical cryptology using methods of number theory, algebra, probability. Topics include symmetric and public-key cryptosystems, one-way functions, signatures, key exchange, groups, primes, pseudoprimes, primality tests, quadratic reciprocity, factoring, rho method, RSA, discrete logs. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra for Applications
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 110A. Integers, congruences; fields, applications of finite fields; polynomials; permutations, introduction to groups.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Methods of Data Theory
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to computational methods for data problems with focus on linear algebra and optimization. Matrix and tensor factorization, PageRank, assorted other topics in matrices, linear programming, unconstrained optimization, constrained optimization, integer optimization, dynamic programming, and stochastic optimization. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry
courses.comments: 120A is requisite to 120B.
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Course Curves in 3-space, Frenet formulas, surfaces in 3-space, normal curvature, Gaussian curvature, congruence of curves and surfaces, intrinsic geometry of surfaces, isometries, geodesics, Gauss/Bonnet theorem. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Curves in 3-space, Frenet formulas, surfaces in 3-space, normal curvature, Gaussian curvature, congruence of curves and surfaces, intrinsic geometry of surfaces, isometries, geodesics, Gauss/Bonnet theorem. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Topology
courses.description: Metric and topological spaces, completeness, compactness, connectedness, functions, continuity, homeomorphisms, topological properties.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Foundations of Geometry
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Axioms and models, Euclidean geometry, Hilbert axioms, neutral (absolute) geometry, hyperbolic geometry, Poincaré model, independence of parallel postulate.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Analysis
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Recommended: course 115A. Rigorous introduction to foundations of real analysis; real numbers, point set topology in Euclidean space, functions, continuity. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Analysis (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: courses 32B and 33B, with grades of B or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Recommended: course 115A. Honors course parallel to course 131A. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Analysis
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Derivatives, Riemann integral, sequences and series of functions, power series, Fourier series. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Analysis (Honors)
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Honors course parallel to course 131B. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topics in Analysis
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Advanced topics in analysis, such as Lebesgue integral, integration on manifolds, harmonic analysis. Content varies from year to year. May be repeated for credit by petition.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Complex Analysis for Applications
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to basic formulas and calculation procedures of complex analysis of one variable relevant to applications. Topics include Cauchy/Riemann equations, Cauchy integral formula, power series expansion, contour integrals, residue calculus.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Complex Analysis (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: courses 32B, 33B, and 131A, with grades of B or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Specifically designed for students who have strong commitment to pursue graduate studies in mathematics. Introduction to complex analysis, with more emphasis on proofs. Honors course parallel to course 132. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Fourier Analysis
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Fourier series, Fourier transform in one and several variables, finite Fourier transform. Applications, in particular, to solving differential equations. Fourier inversion formula, Plancherel theorem, convergence of Fourier series, convolution. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear and Nonlinear Systems of Differential Equations
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Dynamical systems analysis of nonlinear systems of differential equations. One- and two- dimensional flows. Fixed points, limit cycles, and stability analysis. Bifurcations and normal forms. Elementary geometrical and topological results. Applications to problems in biology, chemistry, physics, and other fields. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Selected topics in differential equations. Laplace transforms, existence and uniqueness theorems, Fourier series, separation of variable solutions to partial differential equations, Sturm/Liouville theory, calculus of variations, two-point boundary value problems, Green’s functions. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Linear partial differential equations, boundary and initial value problems; wave equation, heat equation, and Laplace equation; separation of variables, eigenfunction expansions; selected topics, as method of characteristics for nonlinear equations.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Modeling
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to fundamental principles and spirit of applied mathematics. Emphasis on manner in which mathematical models are constructed for physical problems. Illustrations from many fields of endeavor, such as physical sciences, biology, economics, and traffic dynamics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Methods of Applied Mathematics
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Integral equations, Green’s function, and calculus of variations. Selected applications from control theory, optics, dynamical systems, and other engineering problems.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Experience of Data Science
courses.prereq_text: courses 118, 131A, 156 or Statistics 101C, 170S or Statistics 100B, Statistics 101A
courses.description: (Same as Statistics M148.) Lecture, four hours. Students solve real data science problems for community- or campus-based clients. Students work in small groups with faculty member and client to frame client’s question in data science terms, create mathematical models, analyze data, and report results. Students may elect to undertake research on foundations of data science, studying advanced topics and writing senior thesis with discussion of findings or survey of literature on chosen foundational topic. Development of collaborative skills, communication principles, and discussion of ethical issues. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Applied Numerical Methods
courses.prereq_text: courses 32B, 33B, 115A, Program in Computing 10A or Computer Science 31
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to numerical methods with emphasis on algorithms, analysis of algorithms, and computer implementation issues. Solution of nonlinear equations. Numerical differentiation, integration, and interpolation. Direct methods for solving linear systems. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Analysis Part 1 (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: courses 32B, 33B, 115A, 131A, Computer Science 31 or Programming in Computing 10A or equivalent, with grades of B or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 151A. Rigorous introduction to numerical algorithms including necessary skills to apply algorithms in statistics, imaging, data science, engineering, and related fields. Root finding, solving linear systems, interpolation, quadrature, and finding eigenvalues. MATLAB programming. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Applied Numerical Methods
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to numerical methods with emphasis on algorithms, analysis of algorithms, and computer implementation issues. Solution of nonlinear equations. Numerical differentiation, integration, and interpolation. Direct methods for solving linear systems. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Analysis Part 2 (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: courses 115A or 115AH, 131A or 131AH, 151A or 151AH, Computer Science 31 or Programming in Computing 10A, with grades of B or better
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Rigorous introduction to numerical algorithms including necessary skills to apply algorithms in statistics, imaging, data science, engineering and related fields. Finding eigenvalues, finding numerical solutions to ordinary differential equations, the least squares problem and the fast Fourier transform. MATLAB programming. Honors course parallel to course 151B. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Imaging
courses.prereq_text: courses 32B, 33B, 115A, Program in Computing 10A or Computer Science 31
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Imaging geometry. Image transforms. Enhancement, restoration, and segmentation. Descriptors. Morphology. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.prereq_text: courses 115A, 164, 170A or 170E or Statistics 100A, and Computer Science 31 or Program in Computing 10A
courses.comments: recommended requisite: Program in Computing 16A or Statistics 21.
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Strongly Introductory course on mathematical models for pattern recognition and machine learning. Topics include parametric and nonparametric probability distributions, curse of dimensionality, correlation analysis and dimensionality reduction, and concepts of decision theory. Advanced machine learning and pattern recognition problems, including data classification and clustering, regression, kernel methods, artificial neural networks, hidden Markov models, and Markov random fields. Projects in MATLAB to be part of final project presented in class. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Optimization
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for former Electrical Engineering 136. Fundamentals of optimization. Linear programming: basic solutions, simplex method, duality theory. Unconstrained optimization, Newton method for minimization. Nonlinear programming, optimality conditions for constrained problems. Additional topics from linear and nonlinear programming. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Game Theory
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Quantitative modeling of strategic interaction. Topics include extensive and normal form games, background probability, lotteries, mixed strategies, pure and mixed Nash equilibria and refinements, bargaining; emphasis on economic examples. Optional topics include repeated games and evolutionary game theory. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Networks
courses.prereq_text: courses 115A, 170E (or 170A or Electrical and Computer Engineering 131A or Statistics 100A)
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to network science (including theory, computation, and applications), which can be used to study complex systems of interacting agents. Study of networks in technology, social, information, biological, and mathematics involving basic structural features of networks, generative models of networks, network summary statistics, centrality, random graphs, clustering, and dynamical processes on networks. Introduction to advanced topics as time permits. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability Theory I
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open to students with credit for course 170E, Electrical and Computer Engineering 131A, or Statistics 100A. Rigorous presentation of probability theory based on real analysis. Probability space, probability and conditional probability, independence, Bayes’ rule, discrete and continuous random variables and their distributions, expectation, moments and variance, conditional distribution and expectation, weak law of large numbers. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability Theory II
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Continuation of rigorous presentation of probability theory based on real analysis. Moments and generating functions; laws of large numbers, central limit theorem, and convergence in distribution; branching processes; random walks; Poisson and other random processes in continuous time. Advance topics in probability theory. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics 1: Probability
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Highly recommended: course 61 or 70. Not open to students with credit for course 170A, Electrical and Computer Engineering 131A, or Statistics 100A. Introduction to probability theory with emphasis on topics relevant to applications. Topics include discrete (binomial, Poisson, etc.) and continuous (exponential, gamma, chi-square, normal) distributions, bivariate distributions, distributions of functions of random variables (including moment generating functions and central limit theorem). P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics 2: Statistics
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open to students with credit for Statistics 100B. Introduction to statistics. Topics include sampling, estimation (maximum likelihood and Bayesian), properties of estimators, regression, confidence intervals, hypotheses testing, analysis of variance. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Stochastic Processes
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Discrete Markov chains, continuous-time Markov chains, renewal theory. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics of Finance for Mathematics/Economics Students
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 174A, Economics 141, or Statistics C183/C283. Mathematical modeling of financial securities in discrete and continuous time. Forwards, futures, hedging, swaps, uses and pricing (tree models and Black-Scholes) of European and American options, Greeks and numerical methods. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Theory of Interest and Applications
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Types of interest, time value of money, annuities and similar contracts, loans, bonds, portfolios and general cash flows, rate of return, term structure of interest rates, duration, convexity and immunization, interest rate swaps, financial derivatives, forwards, futures, and options. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Foundations of Actuarial Mathematics: Life Insurance and Annuities
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to mathematics associated with long-term insurance coverages. Single- and multiple-life survival models, annuities, premium calculations and policy values, reserves, pension plans and retirement benefits. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Foundations of Actuarial Mathematics: Additional Topics in Long-Term Actuarial Mathematics
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Multistate models, covers pensions, health insurances, and profit-testing. Study of probability distributions employed most commonly in actuarial theory. Beginning study of short-term actuarial mathematics. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Foundations of Actuarial Mathematics: Loss Models
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Study of loss models associated with actuarial problems. Covers severity, frequency, and aggregate loss models, parameter estimation (frequentist, Bayesian), model selection, and credibility. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Topic in Financial Mathematics
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Continuation of course 174E. In-depth study of risk measures and instruments of risk management in investment portfolios and corporate financial structure. Exotic and real options, value at risk, mean-variance analysis, portfolio optimization, risk analysis, capital asset pricing model, market efficiency, and Modigliani-Miller theory. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Graph Theory
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Strongly recommended: course 115A. Designed for mathematics and computer science and engineering students. Graphs and trees. Planarity, graph colorings. Set systems. Ramsey theory. Random graphs. Linear algebra methods. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algorithms
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for Computer Science 180. Graphs, greedy algorithms, divide and conquer algorithms, dynamic programming, network flow. Emphasis on designing efficient algorithms useful in diverse areas such as bioinformatics and allocation of resources. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Enumerative Combinatorics
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Designed for mathematics and physics students. Permutations and combinations, counting principles, recurrence relations, and generating functions. Application to asymptotic and probabilistic enumeration. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Individual Studies for USIE Facilitators
courses.prereq_text: (Honors Collegium 101E) (may be taken concurrently); and Limited to junior/senior USIE facilitators
courses.description: Tutorial, to be arranged. Individual study in regularly scheduled meetings with faculty mentor to discuss selected USIE seminar topic, conduct preparatory research, and begin preparation of syllabus. Individual contract with faculty mentor required. May not be repeated. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Individual Studies for USIE Facilitators
courses.prereq_text: course 188SA; and (Honors Collegium 101E) (may be taken concurrently); and Limited to junior/senior USIE facilitators
courses.description: Tutorial, to be arranged. Individual study in regularly scheduled meetings with faculty mentor to finalize course syllabus. Individual contract with faculty mentor required. May not be repeated. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Individual Studies for USIE Facilitators
courses.prereq_text: course 188SB; and Limited to junior/senior USIE facilitators
courses.description: Tutorial, to be arranged. Individual study in regularly scheduled meetings with faculty mentor while facilitating USIE 88S course. Individual contract with faculty mentor required. May not be repeated. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Honors Seminars
courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Designed as adjunct to undergraduate lecture course. Exploration of topics in greater depth through supplemental readings, papers, or other activities and led by lecture course instructor. May be applied toward honors credit for eligible students. Honors content noted on transcript. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Honors Contracts
courses.prereq_text: Limited to students in College Honors Program
courses.description: Tutorial, three hours. Designed as adjunct to upper-division lecture course. Individual study with lecture course instructor to explore topics in greater depth through supplemental readings, papers, or other activities. May be repeated for maximum of 4 units. Individual honors contract required. Honors content noted on transcript. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in History and Development of Mathematics
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Number Theory
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Algebra
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Logic
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Geometry
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Topology
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Analysis
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Differential Equations
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Functional Analysis
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Applied Mathematics
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Probability
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Dynamical Systems
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Mathematics
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Combinatorics
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar: Current Literature in Cryptography
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Designed for undergraduate students. Readings and presentations of papers in mathematical literature under supervision of staff member. One-hour presentation required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Variable Topics Research Seminars: Mathematics
courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Variable topics research course in mathematics that covers material not covered in regular mathematics upper-division curriculum. Reading, discussion, and development of culminating project. May be repeated for credit with topic and/or instructor change. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Honors Research Seminars: Mathematics
courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Participating seminar on advanced topics in mathematics. Content varies from year to year. May be repeated for credit by petition. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Collaborative Learning Theory and Practice
courses.prereq_text: course M192A (may be taken concurrently); and Limited to students serving as learning assistants
courses.description: Seminar, two to four hours. Further exploration of current topics in pedagogy and education research focused on methods of learning in small groups and their practical application to supervise learning in UCLA mathematics courses. With instructor's guidance, students apply pedagogical principles based on current education research, assist with development of innovative instructional materials, and receive and generate frequent feedback on their activities. May be repeated three times for credit. May not be used to fulfill elective requirement for any mathematics major. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Collaborative Learning Theory and Practice
courses.description: (Formerly numbered 192A.) (Same as Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences M192A, Chemistry M192E, Computer Science M192A, Life Sciences M192A, and Physics M192S.) Seminar, one hour. Training seminar for undergraduate students who are selected for learning assistant (LA) program. Exploration of current topics in pedagogy and education research focused on methods of learning and their practical application in small-group settings. Students practice communication skills with frequent assessment of and feedback on progress. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Community Internships in Mathematics Education
courses.description: Tutorial, to be arranged. Internship to be supervised by Center for Community Learning and Mathematics Department. Students meet on regular basis with instructor, provide periodic reports of their experience, have assigned readings on mathematics education, and complete final paper. May not be repeated and may not be applied toward major requirements. Individual contract with supervising faculty member required. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Individual Studies in Mathematics
courses.description: Tutorial, three hours per week per unit. At discretion of chair and subject to availability of staff, individual intensive study of topics suitable for undergraduate course credit but not specifically offered as separate courses. Scheduled meetings to be arranged between faculty member and student. Assigned reading and tangible evidence of mastery of subject matter required. May be repeated for maximum of 12 units, but no more than one 197 or 199 course may be applied toward upper-division courses required for majors offered by Mathematics Department. Individual contract required. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Directed Research or Senior Project in Mathematics
courses.description: Tutorial, three hours per week per unit. Supervised individual research under guidance of faculty mentor. Scheduled meetings to be arranged between faculty member and student. Culminating report required. May be repeated for maximum of 12 units, but no more than one 197 or 199 course may be applied toward upper-division courses required for majors offered by Mathematics Department. Individual contract required. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MC&IP
courses.title: Fiat Lux Freshman Seminars
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Discussion of and critical thinking about topics of current intellectual importance, taught by faculty members in their areas of expertise and illuminating many paths of discovery at UCLA. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MC&IP
courses.title: Student Research Program
courses.description: Tutorial (supervised research or other scholarly work), three hours per week per unit. Entry-level research for lower-division students under guidance of faculty mentor. Students must be in good academic standing and enrolled in minimum of 12 units (excluding this course). Individual contract required; consult Undergraduate Research Center. May be repeated. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Experiments in Cell and Tissue Culture
courses.description: (Same as Biomedical Research M6H.) Lecture, three hours; discussion; one hour. Answering important questions in biology often involves executing experiments using cultured cells or tissues in the laboratory. Discussion of the fundamentals of cell and tissue culture, how to carry out successful experiments, and how to work through experimental challenges. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Fiat Lux Freshman Seminars
courses.description: Seminar, one hour. Discussion of and critical thinking about topics of current intellectual importance, taught by faculty members in their areas of expertise and illuminating many paths of discovery at UCLA. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Collaborative Undergraduate Research Laboratory in Yeast, Genetics, and Molecular Biology
courses.prereq_text: Limited to 24 students in Collaborative Undergraduate Research Laboratory (CURL), sponsored by Howard Hughes Medical Institute Professors Program
courses.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, six hours. Basic training in biological research, covering topics in molecular genetics, molecular biology, model organism biology, and data analysis. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Stem Cell Biology, Politics, and Ethics: Teasing Apart Issues
courses.description: Lecture, three and one half hours; discussion, 90 minutes. Developmental biology of various types of human stem cells. Important functional differences between embryonic, hematopoietic, and adult stem cells, as well as differences in their biomedical potentials. Discussion of history of debate surrounding embryos, as well as various social, ethical, political, and economic aspects of stem cell research. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Biomedical Ethics
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Examination of importance of ethics in research and exploration of how and why bioethics is relevant to reproductive screening, policy formation, public regulation, and law. Provides foundation in traditional ethics, consideration of subcategories of bioethics, neuroethics, and eugenics, and how to apply ethics to contemporary issues in research and technology. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Honors Seminars
courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Designed as adjunct to lower-division lecture course. Exploration of topics in greater depth through supplemental readings, papers, or other activities and led by lecture course instructor. May be applied toward honors credit for eligible students. Honors content noted on transcript. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Honors Contracts
courses.prereq_text: Limited to students in College Honors Program
courses.description: Tutorial, three hours. Designed as adjunct to lower-division lecture course. Individual study with lecture course instructor to explore topics in greater depth through supplemental readings, papers, or other activities. May be repeated for maximum of 4 units. Individual honors contract required. Honors content noted on transcript. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Human Stem Cells and Medicine
courses.description: Lecture, three and one half hours; discussion 90 minutes. Stem cells have potential to revolutionize way medicine is practiced today. Some stem cell therapies are already used successfully to treat thousands of people worldwide. Other stem cell therapies are considered experimental; therefore treatments must be monitored by Food and Drug Administration to ensure safety and efficacy. Some stem cell therapies are offered with minimal scientific justification, relying on hope and hype rather than scientific fact. Exploration of use of stem cells in modern medicine to take close look at science behind some of today’s most famous and infamous stem cell medical applications. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Student Research Program
courses.description: Tutorial (supervised research or other scholarly work), three hours per week per unit. Entry-level research for lower-division students under guidance of faculty mentor. Students must be in good academic standing and enrolled in minimum of 12 units (excluding this course). Individual contract required; consult Undergraduate Research Center. May be repeated. P/NP grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Introduction to Cell Biology
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology majors or to students with credit for course 165A. Analysis of cell organization, structure, and function at molecular level. Cell membranes and organelles, membrane transport, cellular signaling, cytoskeleton and cell movement, intracellular trafficking, cell energetics. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Research Immersion Laboratory in Developmental Biology
courses.prereq_text: Life Sciences 3, 4, and 23L, or 7A, 7B, 7C, 23L, and 107; and Limited to Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology and Microbiology, Immunology, and Molecular Genetics majors
courses.comments: 104AL is requisite to 104BL.
courses.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, eight hours. Course Discovery-based research using sea urchins as model system. Students determine expression of unstudied sea urchin genes using combination of molecular biology and computation techniques. May not be repeated for credit. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Advanced Research Analysis in Developmental Biology
courses.prereq_text: course 104AL; and Limited to Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology majors
courses.description: Laboratory, six hours. Investigation to be primarily computational in nature whereby students use bioinformatics or mathematical modeling software to interpret, expand, or refine datasets. Use of graphics software to prepare figures and illustrations for presentations, posters, reports, and websites (database entries). Research accomplishments discussed in weekly seminar-style meetings in which student groups create PowerPoint slides and formally present results to class. Production of team poster and final report describing entire research project required. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Research Immersion Laboratory in Plant Molecular Biology and Biotechnology
courses.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, four hours; outside study, nine hours. Students participate in discovery-based, authentic research projects to examine the expression, accumulation, and/or function of plant genes/proteins using combination of molecular, genetic, and computational techniques. The plant and/or molecular reagents generated are incorporated into the instructor’s ongoing research programs. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Reproductive Science and Health
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Study of the cell, molecular and developmental biology of the reproductive system, and how this impacts reproductive health and pregnancy. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Undergraduate Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology Education Research
courses.prereq_text: course 144, Life Sciences 7A, 7B, 7C, 7L, and Biostatistics 100 or Life Sciences 40 or Psychology 100A or Statistics 10 or 13 or 100A
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours; outside study, 10 hours. Students engage in an authentic biology education research project to understand how biologists can apply the scientific process to study how students learn. Students gain experience exploring biology education research literature, developing research questions, collecting and analyzing data, and communicating their findings. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Fundamentals of Digital Imaging and Image Processing
courses.prereq_text: Life Sciences 7A, 7B, 7C, and Life Sciences 30A, 30B, and 40 or Statistics 13, or Mathematics 3A, 3B, and 3C, or Mathematics 31A, 31B, and 32A or 33A
courses.description: (Same as Computational and Systems Biology M130.) Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours. Digital imaging has become integral tool to our everyday lives and to nearly every field of life sciences. Quantitative approach to learning about basic properties of digital signals and surveying fundamental methods for processing and analyzing images. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Developmental Biology
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Development of understanding of fundamental molecular mechanisms and cellular activities guiding formation of complex organism from single fertilized egg. Development of model organisms to understand conserved nature of developmental decisions across animal kingdom, distinct features that lead to diversification of animal shape and form during evolution. Origin and roles of stem and progenitor cells in development and maintenance of specific organ systems. Roles of cell shape change, cell death, proliferation, and migration in generating shape of embryo, organs, and tissues. Mechanisms by which cells become different from and communicate with one another to coordinate their activities in time and space in embryo. Special emphasis on experimental approaches used to address these fundamental questions that determine how organized tissues and organs are formed and maintained throughout life of organism. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Cancer Cell Biology
courses.description: (Same as Biological Chemistry M140.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Cancer causes and genetics. Effects of cell transformation on cell growth and metabolism. Altered cell cycle, metabolism, and differentiation pathways in cancer cells. Tumor microenvironment contributions to cancer malignancy, including angiogenesis, metastasis, and immune system evasion. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Molecular Basis of Plant Differentiation and Development
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. In-depth study of basic processes of growth differentiation and development in plants and molecular mechanisms underlying these processes. Discussion of variety of plant systems, with focus on developing critical understanding of current experimental basis of research in this field. Concurrently scheduled with course C239. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Design Principles of Biological Circuits
courses.prereq_text: Life Sciences 7A, 7B, 7C, and 107, and Life Sciences 30A and 30B or Mathematics 3A, 3B, and 3C or Mathematics 31A and 31B, and Life Sciences 40 or Statistics 10 or 13
courses.description: (Formerly numbered 142.) Lecture, three hours; laboratory, four hours. Quantitative analysis of genetic circuits that control behavior of biological systems, including prokaryotic model organisms and multicellular developmental systems. Introduction of basic principles of systems biology through specific examples. Application of these principles in designing synthetic genetic circuits. Concurrently scheduled with course C202. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Developmental Biology: Genetic Control of Organogenesis
courses.prereq_text: course 138, Life Sciences 3, 4, and 23L, or 7A, 7B, 7C, 23L, and 107
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Cellular and molecular basis of animal embryology, with primary emphasis on vertebrate organ development, but including pertinent material from Drosophila and other invertebrate model organisms. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Molecular Biology of Cellular Processes
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for Chemistry 153B. Development of thorough understanding of fundamentals of modern molecular biology both from perspective of known molecular mechanisms for regulating fundamental processes in cells and from theoretical applied perspective for using molecular biology as laboratory tool. Special emphasis on molecular mechanisms that relate to chromatin and histone modifications, DNA replication and repair, transposition, microRNAs, meiosis, and splicing. Application of molecular biology as tool to understand embryonic development, reprogramming, cancer, and stem cells. Development of sophisticated understanding of DNA, RNA, and protein as well as capability of designing experiments to address fundamental questions in biology and interpreting experimental data. Letter grading.

courses.subject: MCD BIO
courses.title: Appreciation and Critical Review of Biomedical Research
courses.description: Seminar, four hours.
